Thanks for the packet — reviewed the numbers and policy constraints. Notes:

1) Policy baseline: standard marketplace rev-share is 25% and Net-30 billing. Upfront credits are allowed but treated as vendor allowances and must be amortized; credits that materially reduce near-term cash flow need executive sign-off.

2) Financial impact: with the proposed terms, Redwood NRR impact (first 12 months) approx $165k in foregone rev-share plus $120k cash-offset exposure (timing risk). We can mitigate with a 6-month drawdown schedule for the credit and require a Treated AR schedule (finance holdback clause).

3) Risk: Net-90 without a payment guarantee increases DSO and credit exposure. Recommendation: require a payment instrument (LOC or guarantee) or convert Net-90 to Net-45 with a 60-day warrant to Net-90 if invoice aging criteria are met.

4) Recommended approval ask to execs (Jonas):
  • Approve rev-share of 15% for the first 12 months (then revert to 25%).
  • Approve vendor credit of $120,000 amortized across first 6 invoices, subject to milestone verification and finance holdback.
  • Approve Net-90 for first 6 invoices only if StackScale provides an LOC or trade guarantee; otherwise, Net-45 with conditional escalation to Net-90 at month 3.

5) Docs/legal: marketplace team must update the private offer metadata (term flags) and legal needs to prepare an amendment to the marketplace agreement. Timeline: if exec signs off this week, marketplace listing and DocuSign can be completed in ~10 business days.

I am comfortable recommending this to Jonas with the mitigations above.

—Karthik
